messages:
sofia: Quick check — ran the private VPC smoke suite on node pv-03 and seeing a small tail-latency bump for small-gen workloads (p95 ~ 2.9% higher than baseline). Can someone run a quick compare with and without the IO scheduler change?

james: on it. which kernel/ami and cgroup config did you use?

sofia: pv-03 is ami:v2026-03-01-k8s, kernel 5.19. cgroup v2, kube runtime has cpu.max=200000 400000 and memory.low set. I swapped disk scheduler from bfq -> mq-deadline in the AMI image for the test.

li: can you paste the fio command you used? I want to reproduce locally.

sofia: sure — gist of it:
```
fio --name=smoke-randread --rw=randread --bs=16k --iodepth=64 --size=1G --numjobs=4 --runtime=120 --group_reporting
```
I also run our token-gen trace through the harness (short seq len 128, batch 8).

morgan: perf-bot will collect the p95/p99 series if you push test id to the bench queue. sofia, can you drop the bench id?

sofia: bench id `pv-smoke-2076549999-v1` — pushed now. initial numbers: bfq p95=42ms, mq-deadline p95=40.8ms. Baseline (host AMI v2026-02-10) p95=39.3ms. So delta is small but consistent across runs. p99 delta ~3.7%.

james: hmm small but noticeable. could be cgroup throttling on top of IO. do you have top-level cpuacct stats or iowait breakdown?

sofia: attached brief sample from /proc/stat and iostat during run: CPU idle dips ~4% more on pv-03 with new AMI. iowait up ~1.5%.

li: I'll run the same fio + harness under the same cgroup knobs but with cpuset pinning to confirm NUMA noise. command I use:
```
cgcreate -g cpu,memory:/smoke && cgset -r cpu.cfs_quota_us=200000 smoke
cgexec -g cpu,memory:smoke fio ...
```
should reproduce.

morgan: perf-bot: enqueue `pv-smoke-2076549999-v1` -> flamegraphs + sched hist.

perf-bot: queued job 8921, expected completion ~10m. artifacts: /s3/benchmarks/pv-smoke-2076549999-v1/

sofia: thanks. while that's running, two quick asks: 1) can eng-runtime confirm we didn't flip any host-level tunables (tcp_no_delay etc) in the new AMI? 2) any known regression in our runtime's kv-cache interactions when iowait increases?

james: i'll grep AMI diff and post highlights. if we modified irqbalance or swapped irq affinity it could explain cpu steal spikes.

li: kv-cache behavior shouldn't change with io scheduler alone but if we have slightly higher p99 token latency it could be amplified by batching thresholds. I'll review the batching logs once perf artifacts land.

sofia: perf artifacts are up: /s3/benchmarks/pv-smoke-2076549999-v1/flamegraphs.html (looks like a short spike in softirq handling around 1m mark).

morgan: noticed that too — flamegraph shows higher napi/cpu cycles on eth0 during the run. Could be NIC offload toggle in the AMI. james — did we change ethtool settings?

james: no explicit ethtool changes in our AMI recipe, but cloud-init script toggles offload on older images. i'll diff cloud-init between the two AMIs now.

sofia: if we suspect NIC, quick sanity: run `ethtool -k eth0` on pv-03 and compare to baseline. If RX/TX offloads differ, try toggling to baseline settings and re-run smoke.

li: agreed. i'll also check our runtime logs for batching hysteresis flags — maybe increase the warmup tokens threshold for this instance class temporarily.

sofia: thanks team. will wait for bench job to finish and post the final p95/p99 table. ping me if you want me to repro with cpuset pinned. :thumbsup:
